🌪️ Typhoon Fung-wong (“Uwan”) batters the Philippines and now heads for Taiwan.
With winds up to 230 km/h, the typhoon tore across northern Luzon overnight, leaving several dead and forcing over one million people to evacuate.

📍 Mon, Nov 10 (14:00 PHT)
💨 Winds: 130 km/h, gusts 160 km/h
➡️ Located ~400 km NW of Manila, moving toward Taiwan

Fung-wong will turn north, then northeast, possibly crossing Taiwan between Wednesday and Thursday.
⚠️ Taiwan: expect torrential rain (>500 mm on mountain slopes), flooding, and landslides.
Follow all local warnings and evacuation orders.

HOUSE LEADER URGES SEN. CAMILLE VILLAR TO SHOW INDEPENDENCE, STRENGTHEN SENATE OVERSIGHT ON ENVIRONMENT

House Assistant Majority Leader and Las Piñas Rep. Mark Anthony Santos on Monday called on Sen. Camille Villar to exercise stronger environmental oversight in the Senate and avoid repeating what he described as the lapses of her mother, former Sen. Cynthia Villar.

Santos noted that the Senate Committee on Environment, Natural Resources, and Climate Change was previously chaired by the elder Villar, whose family is engaged in large-scale real estate development. The committee is now headed by Sen. Camille, who has yet to convene a hearing since assuming office as senator in July.

"For nine years, we should have seen stronger oversight, deeper investigations, and decisive policy action to prevent the environmental crises we are facing today," Santos said. "Pero ang nangyari—sunod-sunod na environmental threats, halos walang pananagutan, at lalong lumala ang kalagayan ng kalikasan at mga komunidad."

He pointed out that under the former committee chair's tenure, critics and civil society groups flagged issues such as the defunding of Project NOAH, the country's primary climate-risk mapping program, and the continuation of the Dolomite Beach project despite environmental warnings.

Santos also cited the ongoing deforestation of the Sierra Madre due to mining, quarrying, and development pressures, which he said exacerbate flooding, landslides, and biodiversity loss. He added that unchecked real estate expansion in southern Metro Manila has worsened flooding by reducing natural water absorption.

"Nine years is a long time. Kung may tunay na pagsisiyasat at pagtugon, dapat may malinaw na resulta, may reporma, may pananagutan," he said. "Pero hanggang ngayon, baha pa rin. Nasasaktan pa rin ang komunidad. Nanganganib pa rin ang ating kalikasan."

Santos urged Sen. Camille Villar to "break the cycle" and prove that the environment committee serves public—not private—interests.

"This is a chance to break the cycle. I hope the new chair will prove to the Filipino people that the environment committee is meant to protect the people—not private interests," he said. "Transparency, public hearings, and accountability must be the starting point."

He vowed to continue advocating for stronger environmental policies, including the long-delayed passage of the proposed National Land Use Act (NLUA), which the House approved in the previous Congress but which remains stalled at the Senate committee level.

"Ang laban na ito ay laban ng mga ordinaryong pamilyang lubog sa baha, mga mangingisdang nawawalan ng kabuhayan, at mga kabataang may karapatang mamuhay sa ligtas at malusog na kalikasan," Santos said. "Hindi ako titigil."
